facts: The gradient of the tangent to $y=f(x)$ at $x=x_1$ is $m = f'(x_1)$.
The point of contact is $(x_1, y_1)$, where $y_1 = f(x_1)$.
The tangent has equation $y - y_1 = f'(x_1)(x - x_1)$.
The normal is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of contact, so its gradient is $m_{\perp} = -\dfrac{1}{f'(x_1)}$ when $f'(x_1) \neq 0$.
The normal has equation $y - y_1 = -\dfrac{1}{f'(x_1)}(x - x_1)$ when $f'(x_1) \neq 0$.
If the tangent is horizontal ($m=0$), the tangent is $y = y_1$ and the normal is the vertical line $x = x_1$.
General form is $ax + by + c = 0$, where $a$, $b$ and $c$ are integers and $a > 0$.
steps: Find the point of contact $y_1 = f(x_1)$
Differentiate $f(x)$ to find the gradient function $f'(x)$
Find the normal gradient using $m_{\perp} = -\dfrac{1}{m}$ if required
Substitute into $y - y_1 = m(x - x_1)$ and rearrange to the required form

foundation.question_text:
Find the equation of the tangent to $y = x^2 - 4x + 1$ at the point $(3, -2)$.
Give your answer in gradient–intercept form.

Find the equation of the tangent to $y = 2x^2 + 3x - 5$ at $x = 1$.
Give your answer in gradient–intercept form.

Find the equation of the tangent to $y = x^3 - 2x + 4$ at $x = -1$.
Give your answer in general form $ax + by + c = 0$.

Find the equation of the normal to $y = x^2 + 2x - 3$ at the point $(1, 0)$.
Give your answer in gradient–intercept form.

Find the equation of the normal to $y = 3x^2 - 5x + 2$ at the point $(2, 4)$.
Give your answer in general form $ax + by + c = 0$.
Find the equation of the tangent to $y = x^2 - 6x + 5$ at $x = 3$.
Find the equation of the normal to $y = 4 - x^2$ at its turning point $(0, 4)$.
foundation.solution_text:
$f'(x) = -2x$
$m = f'(0) = 0$
The tangent is horizontal with equation $y = 4$.
The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so it is the vertical line $x = 0$.

development.question_text:
Find the equation of the tangent to $y = 4 - x - 2x^2$ at $x = -2$.
Give your answer in gradient–intercept form.

Find the equation of the tangent to $y = x^3 - 5x^2 + 2$ at $x = 2$.
Give your answer in general form $ax + by + c = 0$.

Find the equation of the normal to $y = \dfrac{1}{3}x^3 - x^2 - 3x + 1$ at $x = 0$.
Give your answer in gradient–intercept form.

Find the equation of the normal to $y = 2x^3 - 4x + 1$ at $x = 1$.
Give your answer in general form $ax + by + c = 0$.

development.solution_text:
$f'(x) = 2x$
$m = f'(2) = 2(2) = 4$
$y - 5 = 4(x - 2)$
$y = 4x - 3$
For the $x$-intercept, set $y = 0 \implies 4x - 3 = 0 \implies x = \dfrac{3}{4}$.
For the $y$-intercept, set $x = 0 \implies y = -3$.
$\text{Area} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{3}{4} \times 3 = \dfrac{9}{8}$

development.question_text: Find the coordinates of the point where the tangents to the parabola $y = x^2 - 4x$ at its $x$-intercepts intersect.
development.solution_text:
$x(x - 4) = 0 \implies x\text{-intercepts are } (0, 0) \text{ and } (4, 0)$
$f'(x) = 2x - 4$
At $(0, 0)$: $m = f'(0) = -4 \implies y = -4x$
At $(4, 0)$: $m = f'(4) = 4 \implies y = 4(x - 4) = 4x - 16$
Intersection: $-4x = 4x - 16 \implies 8x = 16 \implies x = 2$
$y = -4(2) = -8$
Point of intersection is $(2, -8)$.

development.question_text: Find the equation of the normal to $y = x^3 - 3x^2 + 4$ at $x = 0$.
development.solution_text:
$y_1 = (0)^3 - 3(0)^2 + 4 = 4$
$f'(x) = 3x^2 - 6x$
$m = f'(0) = 0$
The tangent is horizontal: $y = 4$.
The normal is the vertical line through $(0, 4)$ with equation $x = 0$.

mastery.solution_text:
$f'(x) = -2x$
$m = f'(1) = -2(1) = -2$
$y - 8 = -2(x - 1)$
$y = -2x + 10$
At $A$ ($y = 0$): $-2x + 10 = 0 \implies x = 5 \implies A(5, 0)$
At $B$ ($x = 0$): $y = 10 \implies B(0, 10)$
$\text{Area of } \triangle OAB = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 5 \times 10 = 25$

mastery.question_text:
The parabola $y = x^2 + bx + c$ has a tangent with equation $4x - y - 1 = 0$ at the point $(3, 11)$.
Find the values of $b$ and $c$.
mastery.solution_text:
$4x - y - 1 = 0 \implies y = 4x - 1 \text{ with gradient } m = 4$
$f'(x) = 2x + b$
$f'(3) = 2(3) + b = 4 \implies 6 + b = 4 \implies b = -2$
Since $(3, 11)$ lies on the curve:
$11 = (3)^2 + (-2)(3) + c$
$11 = 9 - 6 + c$
$11 = 3 + c \implies c = 8$
$b = -2, c = 8$

mastery.question_text:
The line $x + 3y - 20 = 0$ is the normal to the parabola $y = ax^2 + 2x + 1$ at the point where $x = 2$.
Find the value of $a$.
mastery.solution_text:
$x + 3y - 20 = 0 \implies 3y = -x + 20 \implies y = -\dfrac{1}{3}x + \dfrac{20}{3}$
$\text{Normal gradient } m_{\perp} = -\dfrac{1}{3} \implies \text{tangent gradient } m = 3$
$f'(x) = 2ax + 2$
$f'(2) = 2a(2) + 2 = 4a + 2$
$4a + 2 = 3$
$4a = 1$
$a = \dfrac{1}{4}$
$\text{Check point of contact: when } a = \dfrac{1}{4} \text{ and } x = 2, y = \dfrac{1}{4}(2)^2 + 2(2) + 1 = 6$
$\text{Substitute } (2, 6) \text{ into the normal: } 2 + 3(6) - 20 = 0$
